diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\partial^+_v f(x)$ and $\partial^-_v f(x)$ exist as extended real numbers
diagnostic_evidence.tag: cor: representation with A of the specular directional derivative

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed equivalence is false. On $X=Y=\mathbb{R}$, take $f(0)=0$, $f(t)=t a(t)$ for $t>0$, and $f(-t)=f(t)$, with bounded $a(t)$ having no limit as $t\searrow0$ (e.g. $a(t)=10\sin(1/t)$). Then $f(-h)=f(h)$, so the two weights in $\partial^{\sd}_1 f(0)$ are equal and the two difference quotients are $a(h)$ and $-a(h)$; hence the specular quotient is $0$ for every $h>0$ and $\partial^{\sd}_1 f(0)=0$. But $\partial^+ f(0)=\lim_{h\searrow0}a(h)$ and $\partial^- f(0)=-\lim_{h\searrow0}a(h)$ do not exist even as extended real numbers. Thus existence of $\partial^{\sd}_v f(x)$ does not imply hypotheses (H1)-(H2).

failure_location.quote: hold if and only if the specular directional derivative $\partial^{\sd}_v f(x)$ exists
failure_location.tag: thm: representation of the specular directional derivative

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No repair preserves the stated iff. The least lossy repair is to keep only the forward direction (under (H1)-(H2), the displayed formula holds) and to revise or delete the corollaries that claim existence of the specular directional derivative is equivalent to existence of the one-sided derivatives.
issues.overall_effect: The stated iff characterization of specular directional derivatives is withdrawn. Results asserting equivalence between existence of $\partial^{\sd}_v f(x)$ and existence of the one-sided derivatives, and formulas/estimates whose right-hand sides are written solely in terms of $\partial^+_v f(x)$ and $\partial^-_v f(x)$ under only the assumption that $\partial^{\sd}_v f(x)$ exists, become unreliable.

issues.title: False converse: existence of a specular directional derivative does not force one-sided directional derivatives
issues.why_classification: A central equivalence is false and has a concrete oscillatory counterexample; the dependent equivalence corollary and the representation/estimate results that treat one-sided derivatives as automatically available cannot be restored without changing the advertised claim.

diagnostic_evidence.tag: rmk:quasi-MVT
thm: quasi-MVT in normed vector spaces

issues.failure_explanation: The scalar bracket gives $g^{\sd}(t_1)\le g(1)-g(0)\le g^{\sd}(t_2)$. Since the hypothesis only gives $|g^{\sd}(t)|=\|\partial_{v-u}^{\sd}(\|v-u\|_X f(u+t(v-u)))\|_Y/\|v-u\|_X$, this yields $-\sup_t\|\cdot\|\le g(1)-g(0)\le \sup_t\|\cdot\|$ and hence the supremum part. It does not yield $\inf_t\|\cdot\|\le |g(1)-g(0)|$, because the lower bracket may be a very negative $g^{\sd}(t_1)$. Also $g(1)-g(0)=\langle\varphi,f(v)-f(u)\rangle$ can equal $-\|f(v)-f(u)\\|_Y$, so the displayed norm identity is false as written.

failure_location.tag: thm: quasi-MVT in normed vector spaces

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the supremum inequality. For the infimum inequality, prove an absolute-value scalar quasi-MVT or an intermediate-value property for the absolute specular derivative; otherwise restrict the theorem to the supremum bound.
issues.overall_effect: The supremum inequality ineq: quasi-MVT-2 is supported after using absolute values, but the infimum inequality ineq: quasi-MVT-1 is not proved by the cited scalar bracket; the proof's 'similarly' step is unsupported.

diagnostic_evidence.tag: lem: convex function specular derivative and one sided derivatives
lem: convex function specular derivative and one sided derivatives

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma assumes only that $\Omega$ is open and convex and that $f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$. For arbitrary $\mathbf{v}\in\mathbb{R}^n$, the points $\mathbf{x}\pm\mathbf{v}$ may lie outside $\Omega$, so the outer terms $f(\mathbf{x}\pm\mathbf{v})$ are undefined and the $h=1$ bound in the proof is unavailable. The middle ordering $\partial^-_{\mathbf v}f(\mathbf{x})\le\partial^{\sd}_{\mathbf v}f(\mathbf{x})\le\partial^+_{\mathbf v}f(\mathbf{x})$ is valid for all $\mathbf v$ because the one-sided derivatives use sufficiently small $h$.

failure_location.tag: lem: convex function specular derivative and one sided derivatives

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the full chain only for $\mathbf{v}$ with $\mathbf{x}\pm\mathbf{v}\in\Omega$, or assume $\Omega=\mathbb{R}^n$; retain the middle ordering for all $\mathbf{v}$.
issues.overall_effect: The full displayed chain is false as stated for proper open $\Omega\ne\mathbb{R}^n$. The later subgradient theorem uses only the middle ordering, so it survives; the outer finite-difference bounds need a domain restriction.
issues.primary_affected_tag: lem: convex function specular derivative and one sided derivatives
issues.title: One-sided derivative chain is stated for every v in R^n although f(x+v) and f(x-v) need not be defined
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local domain restriction and the substantive ordering used downstream is unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof obtains $\partial^+_{\mathbf v}f(\mathbf{x})\ge \nabla^s f(\mathbf{x})\innerprd\mathbf{v}$ for all directions $\mathbf v$, which for a convex function on an open convex $\Omega$ gives the subgradient inequality relative to $\Omega$. It does not define $f(\mathbf{w})$ for $\mathbf{w}\notin\Omega$, and the earlier definition of $SD f(x)$ was for a function defined on the whole space. Claiming the inequality for all $\mathbf{w}\in\mathbb{R}^n$ therefore requires $\Omega=\mathbb{R}^n$ or an extension of $f$.

diagnostic_evidence.tag: alg:SPEG
alg:SPEG

issues.failure_explanation: The stopping test is inverted: the loop breaks when $\|\nabla^s f(x)\\|>\eta$ and continues when the gradient is small. Thus it can return the initial point although its specular gradient is large, and it need not terminate at an approximate stationary point.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Invert the test, e.g. break when $\|\nabla^s f(x)\\|_{\mathbb{R}^n}\le\eta$, or remove the stopping test and use the iteration cap $K$.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm's stated output contract 'approximate minimizer' is not delivered; the iteration formula and the later convergence theorem are a separate matter.
issues.title: SPEG pseudocode breaks when the specular gradient is large
issues.why_classification: The correction is one logical inequality and causes no loss to the underlying iteration or convergence analysis.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Due to the nonlinearity of specular directional derivatives
diagnostic_evidence.tag: thm: quasi-MVT in normed vector spaces

issues.failure_explanation:
For a finite sum $f= rac1m\sum_j f_j$ and a component index $\xi_k$, the conditional mean of $
abla^s f_{\xi_k}(x)$ is the arithmetic mean of component specular gradients, whereas $
abla^s f(x)=
abla^s( rac1m\sum_j f_j)(x)$ is a nonlinear functional of the sum. The paper itself stresses the nonlinearity and only proves an inequality for sums, not additivity. Hence the required unbiasedness condition is generally not satisfied by the proposed component-gradient oracle.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use an oracle whose conditional mean is genuinely $\nabla^s f(x_k)$, or prove additivity of the specular gradient for the finite-sum objective; otherwise the componentwise efficiency claim must be withdrawn.
issues.overall_effect: The stochastic and hybrid methods' convergence guarantees no longer apply to the proposed componentwise construction, and the advertised saving of computing one component instead of the full objective is unsupported unless a different unbiased oracle for $\nabla^s f$ is supplied.
issues.title: Componentwise stochastic specular gradient is generally not an unbiased estimator of the specular gradient
issues.why_classification: The conditional convergence proof remains valid only after the unbiasedness hypothesis is truly met; for the natural component-gradient oracle this generally fails, and replacing it by a true unbiased oracle can require computing $\nabla^s f$, causing a major loss of the stochastic/hybrid efficiency regime.

issues.failure_explanation: As in SPEG, the loop breaks when the computed component specular gradient has norm larger than the tolerance and continues when it is small, opposite to a stationarity stopping rule.

diagnostic_evidence.tag: thm: convergence of the specular gradient method
thm: convergence of the specular gradient method

issues.failure_explanation: The contradiction needs $\sum_{\ell=L}^\infty h_\ell=\infty$. But $h_\ell=t_\ell/\|\nabla^s f(x_\ell)\\|$, and $\sum t_\ell=\infty$ does not imply $\sum h_\ell=\infty$ unless the specular gradient norms are bounded. The missing standard step is that the SPEG iterates are bounded by the $t_\ell^2$ estimate and a finite convex function on $\mathbb{R}^n$ is Lipschitz on bounded sets, so its subgradients, including $\nabla^s f(x_\ell)$, are bounded there.

failure_location.tag: thm: convergence of the specular gradient method

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the boundedness lemma: bounded SPEG iterates plus local Lipschitz continuity of finite convex functions give $\|\nabla^s f(x_k)\\|\le L$, hence $\sum h_k\ge L^{-1}\sum t_k=\infty$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of $\liminf_k f(x_k)=f(x^*)$, and hence the convergence-to-a-minimizer claim, is incomplete as written.

diagnostic_evidence.tag: thm: convergence of the specular gradient method
thm: convergence of the specular gradient method

issues.failure_explanation: Bolzano-Weierstrass gives closeness only for indices $m$ lying in the convergent subsequence $k_{j_m}$, not for every $m\ge M$. The proof then fixes an arbitrary $m\ge M$ and assumes $\|x_m-\bar x\|<\varepsilon/2$, which is essentially the conclusion being proved. The repair is to choose $m$ itself from the subsequence and then use the tail estimate for all $k>m$.

failure_location.tag: thm: convergence of the specular gradient method

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose $m=k_{j_m}$ large enough that both $\|x_m-\bar x\|<\varepsilon/2$ and $\sum_{\ell=m}^\infty t_\ell^2<\varepsilon/2$; then the displayed tail estimate gives $\|x_k-\bar x\|^2<\varepsilon$ for all $k>m$.
issues.overall_effect: The last passage from a convergent subsequence to convergence of the whole sequence is circular as written, although it is immediately repairable.
issues.primary_affected_tag: thm: convergence of the specular gradient method
issues.title: Final convergence step assumes the whole sequence is already close to the limit
issues.why_classification: The invalid quantification is repaired by selecting the index from the already convergent subsequence; no rate or guarantee is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.tag: thm: convergence of the stochastic specular gradient method
thm: convergence of the stochastic specular gradient method

issues.failure_explanation:
The unbiasedness assumption gives $\mathbb{E}[
abla^s f_{\xi_\kappa}(x_\kappa)\mid x_\kappa]=
abla^s f(x_\kappa)$. A single sampled vector can be zero while the conditional mean is nonzero. Therefore the stated early-exit condition does not imply $
abla^s f(x_\kappa)=0$, which is what is needed to conclude via the deterministic optimality condition that $x_\kappa$ is a minimizer.

failure_location.tag: thm: convergence of the stochastic specular gradient method

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the hypothesis by $\nabla^s f(x_\kappa)=0$, or by $\|\nabla^s f_j(x_\kappa)\\|=0$ for all components $j$ under the unbiasedness assumption.
issues.overall_effect: Only part (a)'s stopping criterion is unreliable; part (b)'s convergence conclusion is unaffected.
issues.primary_affected_tag: thm: convergence of the stochastic specular gradient method
issues.title: Stochastic early-exit clause mistakes one zero sampled gradient for zero mean specular gradient
issues.why_classification: The repair strengthens an early-exit hypothesis locally and does not touch the main convergence proof.
